disputes.summary: Joshi's 2024-2025 preprints claim to complete Mochizuki's IUT proof of the abc conjecture and to show that every objection Scholze and Stix raised (notably around Corollary 3.12) is mathematically false. Scholze and other experts remain unconvinced; the mathematical community has not accepted the combined Joshi-Mochizuki argument as a proof. A 2026 formal-verification effort (the LANA project at ZEN University, using Lean, with an interim report presented July 17 2026) reports narrowing down the specific disputed step (concerning whether a diagram commutes / an isomorphism can be regarded as the identity, in the q-pilot/multiradial-algorithm comparison) but explicitly withholds judgment on whether IUT theory constitutes a completed proof, neither confirming nor ruling out a genuine gap.

summary: Since 26 January 2024, the abc conjecture itself has not moved to accepted resolution. The dominant development is Kirti Joshi's claim (arXiv preprint 'Construction of Arithmetic Teichmuller Spaces IV: Proof of the abc-conjecture', submitted March 2024, with a November 2025 FAQ and a May 2025 'Final Report on the Mochizuki-Scholze-Stix Controversy') that his own Arithmetic Teichmuller Spaces construction supplies the missing ingredient in Mochizuki's Inter-Universal Teichmuller Theory and that every objection Scholze and Stix raised in their 2018/2021 critique is mathematically incorrect. This is a first-written-argument event within the window (first preprint March 2024), but no expert digestion, journal acceptance, or community consensus has followed; Scholze and other experts remain unconvinced, and no source found treats the conjecture as settled. I therefore code this 'claimed' rather than 'resolved' or 'open': a serious, human-authored claim exists and has been publicly circulated for over a year, but the community-acceptance bar for 'resolved' is unmet. The RIMS journal publication of Mochizuki's original IUT papers (2021) predates the frozen revision and is not itself a window event; it is mentioned only as background. Separately, a genuine narrowing of the exceptional-set bound occurred: Bernert, Browning, Lichtman and Teraevaeinen (arXiv 2410.12234, October 2024) improved the count of exceptional triples in a cube of side N from O(N^(2/3)) (a 1962 bound, per de Bruijn) to O(N^(33/50)) -- the first power-saving improvement in over 60 years -- and a related paper ('The abc conjecture is true almost always', arXiv 2505.13991, May 2025) surveys this and related density results. These are real quantitative progress on the abc conjecture's exceptional set, but per the DEEP_DIVE.md rule on existence/infinitude questions, narrowing where exceptions could hide is not itself resolving the (infinitude) question, so I treat this as supporting context for 'claimed' status rather than as an independent 'progress' event overriding it -- the Joshi claim is the more significant event and determines the status field. On AI: I found no AI involvement anywhere in this thread. The Joshi/Mochizuki preprints show no evidence of AI-assisted derivation, and a direct, dated quote from the 2026 LANA project (Johan Commelin, on ZEN University's Mathematics Center's IUT-verification project page) explicitly disclaims generative AI: 'It is essential for our project to distinguish between formal verification and generative AI prediction... In contrast, Lean validates mathematical truth against strict logical rules.' The bound-improvement paper (2410.12234) uses classical analytic number theory plus a linear program (with an appendix noting Python code for the LP) -- a computational-optimization technique, not a machine-learning or AI system, so it does not qualify for any ai_role other than none. Two search hits that surfaced during this research -- an OpenAI model disproving Erdos's unit distance conjecture (May 2026) and a Claude-assisted counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture (2026, Levent Alpoege/Anthropic) -- are unrelated conjectures entirely and are excluded as out of scope for this record.
competing_reading: One could argue the correct status is 'open' rather than 'claimed', on the view that Joshi's claim has gained essentially no traction (Scholze reportedly still unconvinced, no journal has accepted it, and it largely restates a 2012-2021 dispute) and so does not meet even the bar of 'a claim the field is taking seriously enough to evaluate'. Under DEEP_DIVE.md's definition, 'claimed' only requires 'a preprint, announcement or machine-checked certificate that experts have not yet digested' -- Joshi's preprint qualifies mechanically, and the ongoing 2026 LANA verification effort shows the field is at least engaging with the underlying IUT question, which supports keeping 'claimed' over demoting to 'open'. I have kept 'claimed' but flag this as a genuine judgment call.
what_would_settle_it: Either a journal publication of Joshi's completed argument accompanied by expert digestion accepting the combined Joshi-Mochizuki proof, or a further LANA-project report (beyond the July 2026 interim one) definitively locating and confirming (or refuting) the disputed step in IUT theory, would settle whether this moves to 'resolved' or reverts decisively to 'open'.

corrections.why: Joshi's claim is not credible enough to be the event the status rests on. It restates the IUT dispute rather than advancing it: it asserts that Mochizuki's proof is complete once supplemented by Joshi's own construction and that every Scholze-Stix objection is wrong, but no expert has accepted it, Scholze remains unconvinced, no journal has taken it, and the 2026 LANA formalisation project explicitly declines to conclude that IUT is a valid proof. Coding it `claimed` would count the abc conjecture among the window's resolutions on the strength of a decade-old dispute nobody outside it considers settled. The record's own competing_reading proposes `open`. Setting the claim aside leaves a genuine event the record already describes: Bernert-Browning-Lichtman-Teraevaeinen's O(N^(33/50)) bound on exceptional triples, the first power saving since 1962. The agent declined to count it under the existence/infinitude rule, but that rule concerns one more example of an existence claim; this moves a bound on the conjecture's own quantity, the number of exceptions, which is `progress` under 6.1. DEPARTURE FROM THE INSTRUCTIONS, STATED PLAINLY: DEEP_DIVE.md 6.1 codes any undigested preprint `claimed` and the agent followed that correctly. This correction applies a stricter rule: a claim with no expert uptake on a problem whose resolution would be a landmark is set aside like a withdrawn claim, and the furthest genuine event that remains sets the status. Joshi's claim stays in `outcome` and `summary` as evidence.
